items.title: 52263_Sonny Greer oral history interview
items.q: Father Hines had the band there.

ctx.x: at the Grand Terrace with Father Hines Band so there was another girl named May Alex, so she was entertaining around New York, so we were going to the Coast to make "Check and Double Check," Amos and Andy, the biggest thing in radio, wasn't no TV. We made the picture, so we went to Chicago and we played at the Oriental Theatre, yes, and so it was a tossup between May Alex and Irving Mills says, "We should have a female vocalist for this engagement. Ivie Anderson was a very, very cute little brown-skinned girl.

And May Alex was real fair, real fair, but she had been in New York and we used to go see her at the cabaret so Irving Mills -- he liked May Alex, because she was a hell of an entertainer, so he asked Duke and he asked me, he say, I can get May Alex for you, so we say all right, so we lived in a hotel right next door to the Grand Terrace in Chicago, so I'm a cabaret man and I went next door and she was in a show there, and Father Hines had the band there.

I saw this girl, cute brown-skinned girl. Really something, so the Duke say, "What do you think? What do you think of her?" I say, "Man, that's the girl." Now we are going to play these days. May Alex looks too white. I say, "You don't want somebody that look like a white girl in front of the band." I say, "Look at this girl."
